UNITED STATES OF AMERICA
                                   BEFORE THE
                 FEDERAL ENERGY REGULATORY COMMISSION
    PJM Interconnection, L.L.C.                    Docket No. EL26-108-000
                                                          (Consolidated with
                                                  Docket No. ER26-3380-000)



    MOTION TO INTERVENE AND PROTEST OF TESLA, INC., SUNRUN, INC.,

            AND RENEW HOME VPP, LLC D/B/A EVERYDAY ELECTRIC




          Pursuant to Rules 211 and 214 of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission's

("Commission" or "FERC") Rules of Practice and Procedure1, Tesla, Sunrun, and

Everyday Electric (collectively, "Joint Intervenors") hereby submit this Motion to

Intervene and Protest in the parallel Section 206 investigation regarding PJM

Interconnection, L.L.C.'s ("PJM") Reliability Backstop Procurement ("RBP") framework.




                                     I. COMMUNICATIONS



          All communications, pleadings, and orders regarding this proceeding should be

directed to the following designated representative for the Joint Intervenors:

          Jaden D. Crawford
          Tesla, Inc.
          1 Tesla Road
          Austin, Texas 75725
          jadcrawford@tesla.com
          617-872-6568

1

                             II. MOTION TO INTERVENE



       The Joint Intervenors, namely Tesla, Sunrun, and Everyday Electric, are leading

developers, operators, and aggregators of advanced energy technologies, distributed

energy resources (DERs), behind-the-meter energy storage, and automated Virtual Power

Plants (VPPs) operating across the PJM footprint. Collectively, the Joint Intervenors

maintain a coordinated technical framework delivering over 1.0 GW of fast, flexible

residential and small commercial capacity committed directly to the PJM footprint,

capable of alleviating regional grid congestion and support wholesale reliability:

   ● Tesla, Inc. ("Tesla") is an original equipment manufacturer of residential and

       small commercial battery energy storage, and develops and deploys energy

       management software, vehicle-to-grid systems, and behind-the-meter small

       commercial and residential battery networks across PJM states.

   ● Sunrun, Inc. ("Sunrun") develops residential solar-plus-storage systems in the

       region, managing a growing footprint of behind-the-meter battery systems capable

       of injecting energy back to the grid during peak events.

   ● Renew Home VPP, LLC d/b/a Everyday Electric ("Everyday Electric")

       coordinates flexible residential capacity across millions of connected devices in

       PJM states, orchestrating mass-scale, automated household load-shifting and

       advanced vehicle-grid integration.

       As active market participants, technology providers, and creators of regional

virtual power infrastructure, the Joint Intervenors' commercial operations, asset

deployments, and multi-state investments are directly affected by PJM's wholesale


                                             2
 market rules, reliability procurement targets, and forecasting structures. No other party

can adequately represent the distinct commercial and technical interests of the Joint

Intervenors. Accordingly, the Joint Intervenors respectfully request that they be granted

full party status in this consolidated proceeding.




               III. LEGAL PRECEDENT AND THE "RULE OF REASON"



          The Commission has long established that a Regional Transmission Organization

("RTO") cannot shield practices that significantly affect wholesale rates or terms of

service by burying them inside internal business practice manuals. Under the judicial and

Commission "Rule of Reason" doctrine, provisions that "significantly affect rates, terms,

and conditions of service" must be filed in the RTO's tariff.2

          The Commission has consistently applied this doctrine to ensure that PJM's

business practice manuals maintain regulatory transparency and conform with filed tariff

obligations:

      ● The "Significantly Affects Rates" Standard: The Commission has explicitly held

          that when PJM modifies accounting, math, or crediting methodologies within its

          business practice manuals in a way that alters market clearing or procurement

          targets, those rules must be moved to the tariff.3




2
    See City of Cleveland v. FERC, 773 F.2d 1368, 1376 (D.C. Cir. 1985).
3
    See Energy Storage Ass'n v. PJM Interconnection, L.L.C., 162 FERC ¶ 61,296, at PP 111–13 (2018).

                                                   3
       ● Manuals Cannot Alter Substantive Rights: The Commission has firmly declared

          that "manual provisions cannot change or revise tariff obligations" or frustrate a

          market participant's ability to offer compliant capacity.4

          Because the internal, structurally deficient forecasting metrics within PJM Manual

19 directly dictate the total Procurement Target for the multi-billion dollar Reliability

Backstop Procurement framework, they directly and significantly affect wholesale rates

under Docket No. EL26-108-000. Under the Rule of Reason, these practices are squarely

within the Commission's Section 206 jurisdiction.




                                           IV. PROTEST



          The Joint Intervenors respectfully urge the Commission to direct PJM to

incorporate technical modifications to its load forecasting methodologies as part of its

upcoming RBP compliance framework. The Joint Intervenors offer these parameters to

ensure an accurate and cost-effective resource target:

Requirement for Technical Revisions to Account for Injection-Capable and Demand-

Shifting Resources: The operational target for any RBP auction relies directly on the peak

load forecasting methodology governed by PJM Manual 19. As demonstrated in previous

submissions in the related IRAS proceeding (Docket No. ER26-3515-000), including

Tesla’s formal comments filed on September 23, 2026, Manual 19 relies on static

baseline assumptions that treat large new loads as entirely flat, invariable demands. The




4
    See Radford's Run Wind Farm, LLC v. PJM Interconnection, L.L.C., 165 FERC ¶ 61,121 (2018).

                                                  4
 current framework does not fully incorporate advanced forecasting methodologies that

account for the over 1.0 GW capability of the Joint Intervenors' PJM-localized co-located

energy storage networks that are capable both of serving on-site load and grid injections,

and automated demand response and peak-shaving dispatch regardless of whether those

behind-the-meter resources possess grid-injection capabilities5. Accounting for how these

active assets are operating to reduce system peaks through state or utility programs within

the PJM Manual 19 Attachment D demand-offset calculations is necessary to ensure the

regional capacity target reflects actual grid conditions.

      1. Need for Predictable Demand Offsets Across Resource Categories: By omitting

          these advanced, multi-technology metrics from the formal forecasting text, the

          current framework prevents injection-capable behind-the-meter battery networks

          and automated residential demand-response assets from being fully credited as

          offsets to peak wholesale demand. Updating these definitions will ensure PJM

          establishes its reliability procurement targets on an optimized baseline that

          accurately reflects the modern grid flexibility resources actively deployed by the

          Joint Intervenors within the PJM footprint.

      2. Alignment with Advanced Technology Investment Signals: Incorporating clear

          Virtual Power Plant and storage capabilities within peak load forecasts supports

          efficient wholesale market signals. Establishing a transparent methodology

          prevents the unintended penalization of commercial investments in flexible, cost-

          effective technologies, helping to avoid unnecessary, ratepayer-funded capital

          expenditures for traditional backstop infrastructure.



5
    See Energy Storage Ass'n, 162 FERC ¶ 61,296, at PP 111–13.

                                                  5
     3. Supporting the Regulatory Role of State Commissions: In its recent orders, the

        Commission affirmed that state utility commissions hold jurisdictional authority

        over retail energy delivery and large-load grid integration, noting that states play a

        central role in managing localized reliability dynamics.6 To effectively fulfill

        these responsibilities, state regulators require clear visibility into regional

        forecasting data and underlying methodologies. Utilizing the Joint Intervenors'

        proposed technology-specific adjustments to reduce baseline peak load

        projections provides state commissions with the necessary operational

        information to accurately evaluate and support local resource adequacy alongside

        PJM.


                     V. CONCLUSION AND REQUESTED RELIEF



WHEREFORE, the Joint Intervenors respectfully request that the Commission:

    ● Grant full party status to the Joint Intervenors in Docket No. EL26-108-000;

    ● Direct PJM to incorporate into its upcoming RBP compliance filing a

        modification to Manual 19 that transparently subtracts verified, technology-

        specific VPP asset pools, behind-the-meter storage grid injections, and automated

        demand response capacities from its baseline peak load projections regardless of

        whether those behind-the-meter resources possess grid-injection capabilities7; and

      constructive forecasting adjustments.
